column4: The speaker is Wang Jian. An incomplete judgment loses the point that the troops are fit for use.
The question concerns needling and the five evils, without negating their existence.
Imperial reliance on the words matters. The contextual expansion changes self-strengthening into the eunuchs restraining themselves.
The procedure follows unsuccessful treatment and promises immediate hearing. It does not report news to the emperor.
The ministers know and fail to remonstrate; this is disloyal. Broken double negation damages that point.
The question asks what the hair could adhere to if the skin were gone.
The first version makes the military reference and the rhetorical question intelligible. The last retains unexplained classical terms.
Instituting extra rites without cause is inappropriate for governing.
The prince is being addressed. One abbreviated version retains the speaker, exclamation and addressee.
The monarch sends an attendant to visit and intends to recall the man. Repetition or a switched pronoun weakens partial versions.
Those who pass together are fellows. The examiner is the seat-master; calling an office by that name changes the referent.
The envoy is the speaker's own, already departed. One otherwise close version omits the named speaker.
The five cities' forces and the support of the northern population are separate details. The contextual gloss drops the five cities.
Qin sends Wei Ran to Zhao to procure military assistance for Yan against Qi. Sending an envoy to Wei changes the mission.
Short royal finances lead to heavier exactions on the people.
Restoring property and removing Gu from the register are not military actions.
The implements for offense and defense have classifications tied to military power.
Jing She is named, Chu dispatches him and Zhao receives assistance. Grammatical breaks and dropping the name matter.
